title: Painting the floor and naming the shop
target: How to change how a shop in Supermarket Simulator looks: the floor is painted with a tool you hold and saved as a surface of its own, and the shop's name is a networked overlay that sizes itself.
version: 1.6.0 (223), read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A floor box with the floor pattern you want to paint
Enough money put aside for the floor you choose, and for repainting later
A shop name you are happy for the whole crew to see

steps.do: Treat the shop's floor as work you do in the room rather than a setting you switch.
steps.because: the floor is a surface the game keeps and paints, and the work is done with a box you hold (PaintableFloor, FloorBox)

steps.do: Choose from the floor patterns the game ships rather than expecting a free colour picker.
steps.because: floor patterns are stored as their own textures and types (FloorTextureData, FloorTextureType)

steps.do: Expect a repaint to replace the floor you had rather than to stack on top of it.
steps.because: the game keeps the previous floor as a record of its own (OldFloorSaveData)

steps.do: Paint again later without fearing the change is lost overnight.
steps.because: the floor and its box are both saved (FloorSaveData, FloorBoxSaveData)

steps.do: Look for the shop's name over the shop rather than in a corner of a menu.
steps.because: a name is drawn on an overlay of its own (ChangeNameOverlay)

steps.do: Name the shop knowing everyone in a shared shop reads the same name.
steps.because: the customisation behind a name is networked (NetworkCustomizationManager)

steps.do: Type a long name without expecting it to run off the sign.
steps.because: a font sizer fits a name to its space, and text can size itself so a translation of another length still fits (NameFontSizer, LocalizeAutoSize)

steps.do: Treat tidiness as part of how the shop reads to the game, not only to the eye.
steps.because: cleanliness is tracked against the shop's standing (CleaningReputationManager)

commonMistakes: Expecting a colour wheel when the game gives you the floor patterns it ships.
Repainting without knowing the previous floor is kept as a record of its own.
Assuming a name you set stays private to you in a shared shop.
Treating cleaning as cosmetic when the shop's standing is what the game records.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
